problem: Deep RL for goal-driven visual navigation struggles when observations are partial and goals change: goal descriptions (one-hot/word embeddings) carry no information about the agent's state relative to the goal, so policies overfit to seen goals/environments. Prior relation-based methods use external priors (Visual Genome) or need per-sub-goal locomotion policies (BRM).
motivation: Real-world navigation and object search need goal-adaptive agents that generalize to unseen environments and new goals, yet the agent only sees local observations. In many settings, goal relations (e.g., object co-location, room layouts) are consistent, so learning them from the agent's own experience could help infer the state relative to the goal.
key_idea: Learn a Goals Relational Graph via a Dirichlet-categorical model from low-level trajectories, and use graph planning costs to weight candidate sub-goals in a high-level Q-network and to terminate the low-level policy early, in a two-layer HRL.
insight: The relation graph supplies the missing goal-to-state information, so relations rather than architecture drive generalization. In the grid-world ablation, removing relation weighting drops overall SR from 0.74 to 0.40, and removing termination drops it to 0.64. Removing the high-level network (graph planning only) only slightly hurts (0.66), showing observations still matter but the graph carries most of the information.
method: Goals Relational Graph: complete weighted directed graph over goals; edge weight w_ij = E[X_ij] under a Dirichlet-categorical model over events 'goal g_j appears after k low-level steps' (value gamma^(k-1)) or never (0); alpha prior (0,...,0,1).
GRG update: after each low-level rollout toward g_i, count which goals appeared and when, update Dirichlet posterior counts (conjugate update), and recompute w_ij.
GRG planning: the relation of sub-goal sg to final goal g is the max-product path cost C(tau*) over the graph.

High-level network: Q-learning (Double DQN) that outputs one Q-value per visible candidate sub-goal; the sub-goal input is multiplied elementwise by C(tau*_{sg,g}); binary extrinsic reward; a back-up 'random' sub-goal if no goal is visible.

Termination-aware low-level network: a standard fully observable goal-conditioned policy (DQN in the grid-world, A3C in object search) with intrinsic binary reward, terminated when any goal on the optimal GRG plan other than sg becomes visible, or at N_max^l steps.
Training: curriculum start positions, pre-trained low-level policy, Double DQN, RMSProp; semantic segmentation + depth (predicted from RGB by a DeepLab encoder-decoder in House3D) as observations.

setting.backbone: Small CNN + FC Q-networks (DQN high-level) with DQN / A3C low-level, trained from scratch; DeepLab-style encoder-decoder for segmentation and depth in House3D
setting.training_data: RL in simulation: 100 grid-world maps with 12 goals; AI2-THOR scenes following Scene Priors setting; House3D single environment or 4 training environments; encoder-decoder trained on 100 extra House3D environments' RGB with GT segmentation and depth
setting.observation: Local 7x7 obstacle/goal map (grid-world); first-person semantic segmentation + depth (GT in AI2-THOR, predicted from RGB in House3D), 4-frame history
setting.action_space: Discrete: up/down/left/right (grid); forward/backward/left/right 0.2 m and 90° rotation (House3D)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth semantic segmentation and depth in AI2-THOR; otherwise none

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only, not standard nav benchmarks; metrics are on a 0-1 scale as printed, and the AI2-THOR main table reports gains over RANDOM.
results: HRL-GRG beats DQN, H-DQN, A3C and HRL baselines on unseen grid-world maps (overall SR 0.74 vs H-DQN 0.45), and in House3D unseen goals in a single environment (SR 0.79 vs best baseline 0.27). In AI2-THOR it improves over Random by more than Scene Priors, e.g. unseen env/unseen goals +0.38 SR vs +0.12. In multi-environment House3D unseen environments SR is 0.62, only marginally above Random's 0.60, though SPL is higher (0.10 vs 0.05).
limitations: Evaluated only on synthetic grid-world and simulated object search with categorical goals; no real robot or standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks
Assumes a stable goal-relation structure and that goals are observable via a semantic recognizer Φ; House3D unseen-environment SR (0.62) is barely above Random (0.60)
Requires enumerable discrete goal space and separate pre-training of the low-level policy; no comparison with more recent ObjectNav methods
